lead: Meat and poultry a household buys, by animal (beef, pork, lamb and goat, poultry, game, other meats) and then by preserved form (cured hams and whole muscles, sausages by tradition, deli and tinned meats), with cuts under their regional names and graded, breed and protected-origin products as archetypes.

b.v: protected origin (PDO/PGI, Japanese brand wagyu) > named breed > generic
b.w: Protected names and breed registries are the main premium filters across meat; breeds link to the animal breeds register.
Grass-fed, grain-finished, free-range, organic and acorn-fed (bellota) claims; label claims, not grades.
Dry-ageing for beef and game, cure time for hams; longer is dearer, not always better.

depts.ax: Is it chosen by named origin or breed, or by the cut and the cooking it suits (grill, roast, slow-cook, grind), or is it veal or offal?
depts.note: Tier for everyday cuts (named by regional cut chart), variety for graded, breed and branded beef.

x.d: Mycoprotein from Fusarium venenatum, the first fungal meat alternative sold to the public.
Whole-cut mycelium steaks and fillets grown from Neurospora crassa.
Fungal protein from an extremophile fungus found in Yellowstone.

k.a: wheat gluten · wheat meat · mianjin · 麵筋 · fu · kaofu · milgogi · mì căn
k.d: Chewy meat-like food made from washed wheat gluten, simmered, steamed, baked or fried.

x.d: Chinese wheat gluten, recorded since the 6th century, made in baked, fried and steamed forms.
Japanese wheat gluten, fresh or dry-baked.
Wheat gluten seasoned and shaped as a duck or poultry substitute.

ax: Which animal does the meat come from, and is it sold fresh as a cut or preserved, cooked or made into a product?
key: 1. Is it made from plants, fungus or wheat gluten to stand in for meat? → Meat alternatives
2. Is it ground meat in a casing, sold as a sausage, pudding or salami? → Sausages & salami
3. Is it a pâté, rillette, confit, tinned meat or other ready-cooked meat? → Deli, cooked & tinned meats
4. Is it a ham, bacon, cured muscle or dried meat? → Ham, bacon & cured meats
5. Is it fresh or frozen beef or veal? → Beef & veal
6. Is it fresh or frozen pork? → Pork
7. Is it fresh or frozen lamb, mutton or goat? → Lamb & goat
8. Is it a farmed chicken, turkey, duck or goose, or its liver? → Poultry
9. Is it a hunted deer, wild bird, hare, rabbit or boar? → Game
10. Is it horse, bison, kangaroo, crocodile, insects or a mixed meat box? → Other meats

Precedence: preserving or cooking beats the animal, so a cured pork leg is a ham (step 4) before it is pork (step 6); a sausage is a sausage (step 2) whatever the meat; foie gras is poultry (step 8) when raw and deli (step 3) when prepared.
